title: Derived constant realization commutes with derived scalar extension
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $q:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, with induced map $\underline q:\underline R\to\underline S$ of constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the derived constant realizations $c_R:D(R)\to D(\mathcal C,\underline R)$ and $c_S:D(S)\to D(\mathcal C,\underline S)$ [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor], derived scalar extension along $q$ and along $\underline q$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] (along $q$ on the one-object site with only the identity covering), and restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For every $M\in D(R)$ there is an isomorphism $$\kappa_M:c_R(M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\underline R}\underline S\xrightarrow{\sim}c_S(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RS)$$ in $D(\mathcal C,\underline S)$, natural in $M$, with the following properties. (1) If $K^\bullet$ is a K-flat complex of $R$-modules with flat terms representing $M$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then $c_R(K^\bullet)$ (termwise constant sheaves) is a K-flat complex of $\underline R$-modules with flat terms, and $\kappa_M$ is represented by the termwise isomorphism $c_R(K^p)\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S\cong c_S(K^p\otimes_RS)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] induced by the identity of the constant presheaves with value $K^p\otimes_RS$. (2) Under $\kappa_M$ and the identification of $c_S$ followed by restriction to $\underline R$ with $c_R$ followed by restriction to $R$, the realization $c_R$ of the scalar-extension unit $M\to M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RS$ is the scalar-extension unit $c_R(M)\to c_R(M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\underline R}\underline S$. (3) For a further homomorphism $S\to T$, the isomorphisms $\kappa$ for $R\to S$, $S\to T$ and $R\to T$ are compatible with the canonical transitivity isomorphisms $(-\otimes^{\mathbf L}S)\otimes^{\mathbf L}T\cong-\otimes^{\mathbf L}T$ on both sides. No boundedness, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Establish the actual ordinary and derived restriction adjunctions before constructing their mates. For ordinary exactness, compose restriction with the faithful functor to abelian sheaves: the composite is the same underlying-sheaf functor as before restriction, and this functor preserves and reflects finite limits and colimits. The ordinary tensor adjunction is the explicit sheafified tensor adjunction of lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction; no derived change-of-rings construction is needed for this ordinary instance. The sheaf derived adjunction follows by applying the coefficient theorem to the everywhere-defined homotopy derived pair. On ordinary modules use lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-scalar-adjunction. For independently chosen localization sizes, conjugate the common-size derived restriction by the canonical Localization.uniq equivalences; compare the composite factorization on cochain complexes and use localization full faithfulness to identify it with actual exact derived restriction. Naturality of both comparison maps follows by applying the adjunction Hom bijection, then naturality of the scalar unit and restriction comparison. The normalized constant-restriction comparison remains the original sheafification argument in Step 6. Ordinary restriction composition is the sectionwise identity: functoriality of constant ring sheafification identifies its scalar actions, and sectionwise extensionality proves its uniqueness.

Construct the geometric morphism $p:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sets}$ without assuming a terminal object of $\mathcal C$. Its inverse image sends a set $E$ to its constant sheaf; its direct image sends $F$ to the set of compatible families $(s_U\in F(U))_U$. A map from the constant presheaf $E$ to $F$ is exactly a function from $E$ to this set of families. The sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] therefore gives $p^{-1}\dashv p_*$. The constant-presheaf functor preserves finite limits objectwise, and sheafification preserves them by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]; thus $p^{-1}$ preserves finite limits. Applied to ring and module operations this inverse image is precisely the constant ring and module sheaf construction [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. In particular the ringed morphism $p_R:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\underline R)\to(\operatorname{Sets},R)$ has identity coefficient map, and its module pullback is $c_R$ on modules: the extra tensor factor is removed by $m\otimes r\mapsto rm$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] to $p_R$. For every K-flat complex $K$ of $R$-modules with flat terms, $c_R(K)$ is K-flat over $\underline R$ with flat terms. The point is presented by the one-object identity-covering site, whose module sheaves are ordinary modules, so the lemma applies to precisely the unbounded complexes in the statement. For arbitrary $M$, choose such a representative $K\to M$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on that point site. Exact termwise realization [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] identifies $c_R(M)$ with the class of $c_R(K)$. This proves the K-flat preservation assertion of (1), without requiring flatness of $q$.

For an R-module A, construct the inverse of the ordinary comparison using the two adjunction universal properties. A map from c_R(A) to restriction(N) yields, at each site object V, an R-linear map A to N(V), hence an S-linear map S tensor_R A to N(V), sending s tensor a to eta_S(s) times f(constant(a)). The tensor adjunction gives naturality in V and module sheafification extends this presheaf map to c_S(S tensor_R A). On generators the chosen comparison sends the ordinary scalar-extension unit applied to constant(a) to constant(1 tensor a). These formulas and the scalar action prove that both composites with the constructed inverse are identities: one by the scalar adjunction and constant generators, the other by tensor induction followed by constant generators. This proves moduleComparison_tensor, including its pure-tensor normalization, without the separate sheafification-tensor theorem. Naturality makes the termwise comparisons a chain isomorphism.

By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] the left side of the chain comparison in Step 3 computes $c_R(M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\underline R}\underline S$, because Step 2 gives a K-flat representative. The same lemma on the point site says $K\otimes_RS$ computes $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ in $D(S)$; exactness of $c_S$ [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] then identifies the right side with $c_S(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)$. To descend the comparison, use [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] on the point site: the localization of its full homotopy subcategory of flat-term K-flat complexes is equivalent to $D(R)$. Both complex constructions above invert its quasi-isomorphisms by change-of-rings invariance and exact constant realization. Step 3 is natural on this subcategory, including homotopies since its comparison is additive. Full faithfulness of precomposition with the localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives a unique natural isomorphism $\kappa$ with these components. This also proves independence of the representative and the representative formula in (1).

proof.text: Construct the normalized constant-restriction comparison using module sheafification. The ordinary constant-module unit gives a presheaf map to the restricted constant S-module sheaf; naturality of the constant ring units makes it R-linear. Its underlying map is the additive constant-sheaf unit, hence locally bijective. The sheafification extension is therefore an isomorphism. The sheafification Hom bijection makes constant sections detect equality; this proves naturality and uniqueness with the stated normalization. Localize this exact natural isomorphism to derivedRestrictionIso. The mate definition gives unit compatibility: its transpose is the realized module scalar unit followed by derivedRestrictionIso.inv, and composing with derivedRestrictionIso.hom cancels the latter.

Let $b:S\to T$. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $K\otimes_RS$ is K-flat with flat terms over $S$; this applies equally to $c_R(K)\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S$ on $\mathcal C$. Consequently all comparisons for the three ring maps can be computed using these representatives and the same $K$. Use the normalized transitivity maps of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], both on the point site and on $\mathcal C$. Starting in $(c_R(K)\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S)\otimes_{\underline S}\underline T$, the route through $\kappa_{R,S}$ and $\kappa_{S,T}$ followed by the constant realization of transitivity sends each constant local generator $(x\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $x\otimes b(s)t$ in $c_T(K\otimes_RT)$. The other route, sheaf transitivity followed by $\kappa_{R,T}$, has exactly the same value. The balanced tensor universal property and uniqueness of module sheafification [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] make the chain maps equal. Their localizations are therefore equal, and the localization uniqueness in Step 4 proves the equality naturally on $D(R)$. This is (3). All constructions used unbounded K-flat complexes and small sites only, so no finiteness, boundedness or Noetherian assumption has entered.

General ringed-topos K-flat preservation specializes to the point geometric morphism; this is a homological tool for constant realizations, not an alternative integral-model route.
Existence of unbounded flat-term K-flat representatives on the point site.
General presheaf/module sheafification tensor comparison gives the ordinary comparison with its S action.
Universal property of the induced sheafified module action ensures linearity, restriction compatibility and equality on generators.
General unbounded scalar extension and its K-flat computation on the point and the given site.
Its K-flat homotopy-subcategory localization equivalence supplies descent to all derived morphisms.
Extension and uniqueness of natural transformations through localization.
General coefficient adjunction explicitly normalizes the unit as x maps to x tensor 1; a definition or unnormalized adjunction would not suffice.
Successive scalar extension can use the original representative because its first extension remains K-flat with flat terms.
